extracted.intended_audience: television industry professionals, press, and fans seeking awards/nominations information
extracted.subtask_description: A Television Academy page listing Emmy categories, nominations, winners, credited personnel, and segments for the series Last Week Tonight With John Oliver across multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Scripted Variety Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Award category listed on the page for Last Week Tonight With John Oliver (appears as winner in multiple years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page shows winners and credited executive producers/producing team (e.g., John Oliver, Tim Carvell, Liz Stanton) and the program/network (HBO Max / HBO). No further definition of the category is provided on this page; examples: Winner — Outstanding Scripted Variety Series (2023, 2024, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Picture Editing For Variety Programming (Segment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for picture editing credited to a specific segment of an episode (appears as nominee/winner for various segments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on page include nominated/winning segments such as 'Facebook Content Moderation', 'That Stuff’s American', 'Boeing', 'The Sad Tale Of Henry The Engine'. Editors credited (e.g., Anthony Miale, Ryan Barger). The page lists year and segment but gives no technical criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Picture Editing For Variety Programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for picture editing in variety programming (listed with episode/segment credits and editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include winners like 'Eat Sh!t, Bob!' and 'The Wax & The Furious' with editors credited (Ryan Barger, Anthony Miale). Page lists nominees/winners by year and segment; no explicit scoring guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Directing For A Variety Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing directing for a variety series (nominations list specific directed segments/episodes and director names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Paul Pennolino credited for 'India Elections', 'Afghanistan', 'Union Busting', and other episodes. Page provides year and directed segment but no further explanatory criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Writing For A Variety Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing category for variety series; page lists credited writers/senior writers for wins and nominations across years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show full writing teams credited for winning years (many names listed per year such as Daniel O'Brien, Tim Carvell, John Oliver, etc.). No rubric definition provided beyond listing winners/nominees and credited writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Production Design For A Variety Or Reality Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for production design in variety or reality series, listing production designers and art directors for nominated segments/episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include credited personnel (Eric Morrell, Amanda Carzoli) and segments like 'Mass Deportations', 'Freight Trains', 'Museums'. Page gives examples by year but no technical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Production Design For A Variety, Reality Or Competition Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Variant wording of the production design category covering variety, reality, or competition series (appears in some year entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from 2019/2020 entries where the category name uses this variant; credited designers and set decorators are listed. No further guidance on criteria on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Production Design For A Variety, Reality Or Reality-Competition Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Another variant phrasing of the production design category appearing in the page's historical entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with credited production designers/art directors for specific episodes; included as an example of how category naming has varied across years. No definition provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Technical Direction And Camerawork For A Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing technical direction and camerawork (specific technical crew credited for nominated episodes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example entries credit Technical Directors and multiple camera operators (e.g., Dave Saretsky, Dante Pagano). The page shows which episodes were nominated/won but does not list evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Technical Direction, Camerawork, Video Control For A Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Variant/expanded phrasing of the technical category including video control; appears in multiple year entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page credits technical directors, camera operators, and video control personnel for nominated/winning episodes (e.g., 'Union Busting'). No further explanatory guidance on standards is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Variety Talk Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for overall variety talk series (appears as winner/nominee across several years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists the program and executive producers credited for wins (e.g., 2016–2022 entries). No description of judging criteria is on this page; examples show it was previously the category used for the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Sound Mixing For A Variety Series Or Special
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for sound mixing in variety series or specials with credited mixers and roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include credited mixers (Siara Spreen, Charlie Jones, Steve Watson, etc.) and specific episodes noted. The page lists nominees/winners by year but contains no scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Original Music And Lyrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for original music and lyrics credited to composers and lyricists for a specific song/episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Episode 629 / Song Title: 'Eat Sh!t, Bob' with music and lyrics credits. Page lists nominations in this category but does not define criteria here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Interactive Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing interactive programming initiatives associated with the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists 'Partially Important Productions' and years where the show won or was nominated for interactive program awards (e.g., winner 2018, 2017, 2015). No further criteria specified on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television Academy Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Television Academy recognition listed on the page (the program received a Television Academy Honors award in 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes the honor but provides no definition or judging criteria for the honor itself.
